atoms.text: This guide configures the IAM role FlowTrailDeliveryRole so that the FlowTrail service can write network flow logs into the S3 bucket acme-flow-logs. The grant is made entirely in an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy of acme-flow-logs is left unchanged. Create a policy named FlowTrailWrite with an Allow statement for the action s3:PutObject. Set the Resource element to arn:aws:s3:::acme-flow-logs/flow/AWSLogs/* so the role can write only under the flow/ prefix. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::acme-flow-logs, which FlowTrail calls before its first delivery. Attach the policy to FlowTrailDeliveryRole and confirm that the role's trust policy names the FlowTrail service principal. Because the role and the bucket are in the same account, no bucket policy statement is required for delivery to succeed. Start a test delivery and check that gzip-compressed flow log objects appear under flow/ within 10 minutes. If objects do not appear, review the policies attached to the role in IAM and look for an explicit Deny in a permissions boundary.

This guide configures the S3 bucket acme-flow-logs so that the IAM role FlowTrailDeliveryRole can deliver network flow logs from the FlowTrail service. The grant is made entirely in the bucket's resource-based policy, and no permissions policy for this bucket is attached to the role. Add a statement with Effect Allow and Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FlowTrailDeliveryRole, with the action s3:PutObject. Set the Resource element to arn:aws:s3:::acme-flow-logs/flow/AWSLogs/* so the role can write only under the flow/ prefix. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::acme-flow-logs, which FlowTrail calls before its first delivery. Save the bucket policy and confirm that the role's trust policy names the FlowTrail service principal. Because the role and the bucket are in the same account, the bucket policy statement alone is sufficient for delivery to succeed. Start a test delivery and check that gzip-compressed flow log objects appear under flow/ within 10 minutes. If objects do not appear, review the bucket policy in the S3 console and look for an explicit Deny statement that matches the role.

This guide covers granting the IAM user logharbor-shipper write access to the bucket corp-audit-archive for the LogHarbor agent, which uploads rotated audit logs from on-premises hosts. The permission is defined only in an identity-based policy attached to the user, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a policy named LogHarborUpload and attach it to logharbor-shipper. Include an Allow statement for s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::corp-audit-archive/hosts/*. Add a separate Allow statement for s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::corp-audit-archive, since that action applies to the bucket rather than to objects. LogHarbor splits files larger than 100 MB into multipart uploads, so omitting these actions leaves incomplete parts that continue to incur storage charges. Store the user's access key in the agent's credentials file with file mode 0600. Run the agent in dry-run mode and then upload one rotated file to confirm that it appears under hosts/ with the expected size. Rotate the access key every 90 days and update the credentials file on each host afterward.

This procedure lets the role EdgeLedgerWriter deliver CDN-style request logs into the bucket web-edge-logs while enforcing that the bucket owner receives full control of each object. The grant is placed in an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy stays as it is. In the policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::web-edge-logs/requests/* and attach a Condition block using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control. EdgeLedger sets this ACL header on every upload, so requests that include it match the condition. Requests without the header are not allowed by the policy and fail with an AccessDenied response. Attach the policy to EdgeLedgerWriter and update the delivery configuration to reference the role's ARN. Deliver a batch of logs and run a head-object call on one result to verify that the object is owned by your account. Logs are written in hourly batches with names that include the distribution ID and a UTC timestamp. Monitor the delivery error counter in the EdgeLedger console for the first 24 hours.

The grant is placed in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role carries no permissions policy for this bucket. In the bucket policy, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/EdgeLedgerWriter that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::web-edge-logs/requests/*, and attach a Condition block using StringEquals on s3:x-amz-acl with the value bucket-owner-full-control. EdgeLedger sets this ACL header on every upload, so requests that include it match the condition. Requests without the header are not allowed by the statement and fail with an AccessDenied response. Save the policy and update the delivery configuration to reference the role's ARN. Deliver a batch of logs and run a head-object call on one result to verify that the object is owned by your account. Logs are written in hourly batches with names that include the distribution ID and a UTC timestamp. Monitor the delivery error counter in the EdgeLedger console for the first 24 hours.

This guide gives the role ComplianceReader read access to delivered logs in the bucket tracegate-delivery so that a nightly review job can process them. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a policy named TraceGateRead containing an Allow statement for s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::tracegate-delivery/daily/*. Add a statement allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::tracegate-delivery with a Condition on s3:prefix that limits listing to daily/. TraceGate writes one object per day named with the pattern daily/YYYY/MM/DD/events.json.gz, so the job lists the date prefix and reads each object. Attach the policy to ComplianceReader and ensure the job's compute environment assumes this role. Run the job against the previous day's prefix and confirm that it reads the object without an AccessDenied error. The role has no write permissions, so it cannot alter or remove delivered logs. Review the role's last-accessed data in IAM after 30 days and remove any permission that was not used.

Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no permissions policy for this bucket is attached to the role. Add a second statement for the same principal allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::tracegate-delivery with a Condition on s3:prefix that limits listing to daily/. TraceGate writes one object per day named with the pattern daily/YYYY/MM/DD/events.json.gz, so the job lists the date prefix and reads each object. Save the policy and ensure the job's compute environment assumes this role. Run the job against the previous day's prefix and confirm that it reads the object without an AccessDenied error. This guide authorizes the role LogSweepRole to remove expired log objects from the bucket pipeline-logs-prod as part of a retention job. The permissions are defined in an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy of pipeline-logs-prod remains unchanged. Create a policy named LogSweepDelete that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::pipeline-logs-prod with a Condition limiting s3:prefix to delivered/. Add a statement allowing s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::pipeline-logs-prod/delivered/*. The PipeSpool delivery service writes new logs to the same prefix, and the sweep job only deletes objects older than 45 days based on the LastModified timestamp. Attach the policy to LogSweepRole and configure the job to assume it. Run the job in report-only mode first and compare the list of matched keys against your retention schedule. Switch to delete mode once the report shows only objects older than the cutoff. Confirm in the access records that no delete request targets keys outside delivered/.

This guide sets up regional delivery of load balancer access logs so that each of three regional roles writes only to its own prefix in the bucket global-lb-logs. Access is granted through identity-based policies, one per role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create the roles RelayGateEU, RelayGateUS, and RelayGateAP, each with a policy that allows s3:PutObject on a single prefix such as arn:aws:s3:::global-lb-logs/eu/*. Use eu/, us/, and ap/ as the three prefixes so that a role cannot overwrite another region's logs. Each policy also allows s3:GetBucketAcl on arn:aws:s3:::global-lb-logs, which RelayGate checks when validating the destination. Set the destination in each regional RelayGate configuration to the bucket name and the matching prefix. Trigger a test delivery in every region and verify that a test object appears under the correct prefix. Check that an attempted upload by RelayGateEU to us/ is rejected with AccessDenied. Document the three role ARNs in your runbook so that later changes remain consistent.

This guide covers granting the role SpoolRunner the permissions to write a verification object and then log files into the bucket batch-run-logs for the JobSpool service. The permissions are defined only in an identity-based policy attached to SpoolRunner, and the bucket policy is not changed. JobSpool writes a zero-byte object named spool-check.txt to the bucket root when you save a destination, and it then delivers logs under runs/. Create a policy named JobSpoolDeliver with an Allow statement for s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::batch-run-logs/spool-check.txt and arn:aws:s3:::batch-run-logs/runs/*. Add an Allow statement for s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::batch-run-logs. Attach the policy to SpoolRunner and select the role when you create the destination in JobSpool. Save the destination and confirm that spool-check.txt appears in the bucket. Run a sample job and verify that its log file appears under runs/ with a name that includes the job ID. If the destination fails validation, compare the resource ARNs in the policy against the bucket name for typographical differences. Delete spool-check.txt after validation only if your own cleanup process requires it.

This guide configures the role DbTraceExporter so that the DbTrace service can deliver database query logs into the bucket db-query-logs, using a role in the same account as the bucket. The grant is made only in an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is left alone. Create a policy named DbTraceExport allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::db-query-logs/queries/*. Add a statement allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::db-query-logs, which DbTrace uses to avoid overwriting existing files when a delivery is retried. Attach the policy to DbTraceExporter and add the DbTrace service principal to the role's trust policy. Set the export interval to 5 minutes, which results in roughly 288 objects per day under queries/. Enable the export and wait for the first interval to complete. Download one object and check that its entries are newline-delimited JSON with a timestamp field. If the export reports a permissions error, check the role's policy for a mismatch between the prefix in the policy and the prefix in the DbTrace configuration. Keep the role's policy limited to the single prefix.
